body:
SLICE 2c BUILT, NOT WALKED (PR of branch task/N-27-slice2c-ref-gone; lead, 15 Nov 2026), and THE ADVISOR'S ANSWERS to the three open questions of the design: (1) tombstone EVERY retired ref (a phone's tap rows point at junk refs too, so one signal means 2b needs no age guess); (2) 90 and 60 days (2d) are fixed constants, not Host settings, and ONCE 2d answers for a missing playlist or entry as deleted, the change_log row is what protects an away phone, not the horizon: the horizon is only a support margin and matters for correctness only if change_log is ever pruned (write that dependency into 2d); 2d TRAP: today's changes query matches on id AND owner, so synthesize "deleted" ONLY when NO row with that id exists at all, otherwise a member of a collaborative playlist is told a live shared playlist was deleted (a 2d test); (3) 2b needs no drawing: the only visible effect is an existing row going away. 2b MUST CARRY ONE TEST: after 2e, a downloaded song whose server file was removed becomes gone: its row stays (the downloads guard), it still plays offline, and clearing file_id does not change how its download is found.
WHAT 2c DOES: migration 0015 (table ref_gone: seq, ref_id unique, at; no foreign key; never purged); the janitor writes one tombstone for every ref it retires in the SAME transaction (a failing pass leaves none: tested across statements); GET library/files?goneSince= adds gone [{id, seq}], goneCursor, goneMore (paged like merges; without the parameter: [], "0", false, so an old phone has nothing to act on); the feature `ref-gone` in info; ref_gone.ref_id classified in the janitor's NOT_POINTERS (its name guard went red first and was NOT weakened); the saved real responses app/test/fixtures/server/library-files-with-merges.json (three keys added) and library-files-with-gone.json (new, for 2b's parser). THE MIGRATION GUARD (advisor's blind spot): helper-n26 has 0014 on its branch and this slice takes 0015 on purpose, because two branches from one main both see the next number as free and, on a database that ran the first, the second counts as already applied and its table is missing at run time with no error. Migrate now REFUSES TO START when two steps share a number, in words (test red first: today it failed with a cryptic UNIQUE constraint, and silently on a migrated database). THE OTHER BLIND SPOT, said plainly: slice 2a has been retiring refs WITHOUT tombstones since #77 was deployed on VM 108; the janitor logs counts, not ids, so any ref it retired before 2c is deployed can never be told to a phone. Only the test phones are affected and VM 108 is usually stopped: log it if VM 108 runs again before 2c is on it. The janitor STILL keeps file_history in 2c (2e lifts it after 2b).
